title: fastpath: add gating and safe-mode fallback with precision toggle for KV-batching
author: Avery Chen
description: Introduce a configurable fast-path gating layer and a runtime 'safe-mode' fallback to the slow (verified) kernel for KV-batching/continuous batching workloads. Motivation: intermittent correctness issues and rare numeric mismatches were observed under aggressive FP16 fast-path kernels combined with continuous batching and concurrent KV updates. This PR adds: 1) a lightweight gating heuristic that disqualifies the fast-path when sequence/kv/attention patterns exceed verified thresholds; 2) a precision toggle (fp16/bf16/auto) exposed on the serving config so ops can opt for safer numeric paths; 3) a cluster-configurable safe-mode flag to force slow-path execution for canary customers or when regressions are detected; 4) additional KV-cache validation hooks to ensure prefix invariants under batching; 5) telemetry and regression metrics to measure fast-path fallbacks and correctness incidents. The description below explains design tradeoffs: the gating thresholds favor correctness at the expense of a small fraction of requests moving to the slow path; precision toggle supports aggressive fp16 for cost-sensitive workloads while allowing bf16 for correctness-sensitive routes; safe-mode provides an operational knob during rollouts and incident recovery. Includes unit and integration tests plus end-to-end microbenchmarks demonstrating latency and throughput impact and a migration guide for model teams.

notes: Design tradeoffs: gating minimizes incorrect fast-path activation while preserving majority perf win; safe-mode is an operational control for incident recovery; precision toggle allows per-route cost/correctness tuning.
